## What are Gmail labels?


Gmail labels are tags that help you categorize your email messages. You can apply as many as you want to a single message and nest them like subfolders. They live in the left sidebar of your Gmail, making it easy to filter your inbox by label with a single click.


### Gmail labels vs. folders: What's the difference?


There are a few key differences between Gmail labels and folders.


-


**Gmail labels don't move your emails.** When you apply a folder to an email, Gmail automatically moves your selected email(s) to that folder. Gmail labels, on the other hand, leave your emails where they are.


-


**You can apply multiple Gmail labels to one email.** You can apply multiple labels to a single email, but you can't store the same email in multiple folders.


-


**Gmail labels are nestable.** You can create sub-labels the same way you'd create subfolders, which is useful for keeping related categories grouped without cluttering your sidebar.


## How to create Gmail labels on desktop


Before you can apply labels to emails in Gmail, you need to create them (unfortunately,[Gemini for Gmail](https://vendors.selectsoftwarereviews.com/redirect/1767832546892x707334240001589200?p=1715808885462x244895206427328500) can't do it for you—yet). There are three ways to do this from your desktop.


### Option 1: Create a Gmail label from the *Labels* list


1.


In the side panel of your Gmail, click the **Create new label** icon, which looks like a plus sign (` +` ) next to *Labels* .


2.


In the popup that appears, enter your new label name, choose a parent label to nest it under, if applicable, and click **Create** .


### Option 2: Create a Gmail label from your settings


1.


Click the settings cog icon (top-right corner), and select **See all settings** .


2.


Click the **Labels** tab.


3.


Scroll down to *Labels* , and click **Create new label** .


4.


### Option 3: Create a Gmail label from an email


1.


Open an email message that you want to apply a label to.


2.


In the menu bar above your message, click the **Labels** icon (it looks like an arrow), and then select **Create new** .


3.


In the popup that appears, enter your new label name, choose a parent label to nest it under if applicable, and click **Create** .


## How to create Gmail labels on mobile


Unlike desktop, there's only one way to create Gmail labels on mobile. (The method is the same for iPhone and Android—I'm using an iPhone.)


1.


Open your Gmail app.


2.


Tap the menu (` ≡` ) in the top-left corner.


3.


Scroll down to *Labels* and tap **Create new** at the bottom of your list of labels.


4.


Enter a new label name.


5.


Tap **Save** .


## How to automatically label emails in Gmail on desktop


Now that you've created labels, here's the easiest way to automatically label emails in Gmail on desktop.


1.


In the Gmail search box at the top of your inbox, click **Show search options** (it looks like three bars stacked horizontally).


2.


Start typing in the search criteria you'd like to apply your new[Gmail filter](https://zapier.com/blog/gmail-filters/) to. You can refine your search using the other filter fields here as well, such as adding keywords to *Has the words* or *Subject* .


3.


After you've added all your parameters, click **Create filter** .


4.


In the window that reads *When a message is an exact match for your search criteria* , click the dropdown next to *Apply the label* and choose the label you want to apply.


This is where you could also check, for example, *Skip the Inbox (*[Archive](https://zapier.com/blog/where-is-archive-in-gmail) *it)* if you wanted to auto-label an email *and* send it straight to a folder without it coming through your inbox. Or *Also apply filter to ## matching conversations* to apply Gmail labels retroactively.


5.


Click **Create filter** .


Now, Gmail will automatically apply your chosen label to any email that matches your given parameters as soon as they hit your inbox.


## How to automatically label emails in Gmail on mobile


If you want to automatically label emails in Gmail from your phone, let me stop you right there—you don't want that. It's much more user-friendly to set this up from your desktop. But far be it from me to keep you from running a mile to go a block.


1.


Make sure you've already created the Gmail label you want to apply. (If you haven't, here'show to do this from your phone .)


2.


Open the Gmail mobile app.


3.


Tap the menu icon (` ≡` ) in the top-right corner.


4.


Tap **Settings** .


5.


Tap **Inbox customizations** .


6.


Tap **Labels** .


7.


Select the label you want to apply.


8.


In the *From* field, enter the name or email of the sender whose emails you want to automatically label.


You can also tap **Add** , and then tap **And** to add a few other filters, including *To* , *Subject* , *Includes* , and *Excludes* .


9.


Once you've added all your parameters, tap **Save** .


## How to manage Gmail labels


You can manage your labels in the *Labels* list found in the left-hand panel of your Gmail on desktop.


-


**Display all emails associated with a label** . Click any label and Gmail will display only emails tagged with that label in the main area of your inbox.


-


**View nested labels** . Click the **Expand** icon, which looks like an arrow, next to the parent label to expand or minimize nested labels.


-


**Color-code your labels** . Click the kebab menu (` ⋮` ) next to a Gmail label > **Label color** > select a color or add a custom one.


-


**Edit and add labels** . The kebab menu also lets you do a number of other things with your label—for example, you can edit the label, add a sub-label, and decide if your label appears in emails in your inbox. (Note: You can't do this on the mobile app.)


## How to delete labels in Gmail on desktop


To delete a label in Gmail on desktop, you have two options.


### How to delete labels in Gmail from your inbox


1.


Hover over the label name in the *Labels* list, and click kebab menu (` ⋮` ) next to it.


2.


Click **Remove label** .


3.


In the popup confirming that you want to delete the label, click **Delete** .


### How to delete labels in Gmail from your settings


1.


Click the settings cog icon, and click **See all settings** .


2.


Click the **Filters and Blocked Addresses** tab.


3.


Click **delete** next to the label you want to delete.


4.


Click **OK** to confirm.


## How to delete labels in Gmail on mobile


There's only one way to delete labels in Gmail from the mobile app.


1.


Tap the menu icon (` ≡` ) in the top-right corner.


2.


Tap **Settings** .


3.


Tap **Inbox customizations** .


4.


Tap **Labels** .


5.


Tap the label you want to delete.


6.


Tap **Delete \[name of label\]** .


7.


Tap **Delete** again to confirm.

## Gmail labels: FAQ


We've covered the basics of how to automatically label emails in Gmail, but you might still have a few lingering questions. Here are answers to some of the most commonly asked ones.


### Can Gmail automatically label emails?


Yes, it can. Here's how to set things up:on desktop oron mobile .


### Are labels applied to existing emails retroactively?


Not by default, but you can tell Gmail to do so. Follow the instructions toautomatically label emails in Gmail on desktop (it doesn't work via mobile) and be sure to check *Also apply filter to ## matching conversations* in step 4.


### Does deleting labels in Gmail delete emails?


No, deleting a label in Gmail only removes the tag—the associated emails stay in your inbox.
